indeterminate forms beyond 0/0: Limit forms like 0·∞, ∞−∞, 1^∞, 0^0, and ∞^0 that must be rewritten as 0/0 or ∞/∞ first.
arc length in parametric form: The length of a parametric curve, given by ∫√(x'² + y'²) dt.
dy/dx for polar: The slope of a polar curve, (r'sinθ + r cosθ)/(r'cosθ − r sinθ).
horizontal / vertical tangents: Tangents where dy/dθ = 0 (horizontal) or dx/dθ = 0 (vertical) on a parametric or polar curve.
arc length for polar: The length of a polar curve, given by L = ∫√(r² + (dr/dθ)²) dθ.
area in polar: The area enclosed by a polar curve, given by A = ½∫r² dθ.
area under parametric curve: The area under a parametric curve, given by A = ∫y(t)x'(t) dt.
convergence/divergence: Whether an integral or series approaches a finite value or fails to.
type i: An improper integral over an infinite interval, defined as a limit of definite integrals.
type ii: An improper integral whose integrand is discontinuous, handled by taking a limit at the discontinuity.
area between polar curves: The area between two polar curves, given by A = ½∫(r_outer² − r_inner²) dθ.
cartesian: The arc length of y = f(x), given by L = ∫√(1 + [f'(x)]²) dx.
parametric: The arc length of a parametric curve, given by L = ∫√(x'² + y'²) dt.
polar: The arc length of a polar curve, given by L = ∫√(r² + (dr/dθ)²) dθ.
graphing common polar curves: Sketching standard polar shapes such as rose curves, limaçons, cardioids, and spirals.
symmetry tests in polar: Tests checking polar symmetry by replacing θ with −θ or π−θ.
alternating series error bound: The error of an alternating series is at most the size of the first omitted term.
alternating series test: An alternating series converges if its terms decrease in magnitude toward zero.
common maclaurin series: Standard Maclaurin expansions for e^x, sin x, cos x, 1/(1−x), and ln(1+x).
error analysis: Determining when a Taylor approximation is accurate enough for a given purpose.
geometric series: A series Σarⁿ that converges only when |r| < 1, to the sum a/(1−r).
lagrange error bound: A bound on Taylor remainder: |error| ≤ M·|x−a|^(n+1)/(n+1)!, with M the max of |f^(n+1)|.
monotone convergence theorem: A sequence that is bounded and monotone must converge.
p-series: A series Σ1/nᵖ that converges only when p > 1.
taylor series centered at a: An expansion Σ[f^(n)(a)/n!](x−a)ⁿ of a function about the point a.
